source_text: Quod omnes Apostoli vel Prophetae non plene sancti definiantur a nobis, sed in comparatione peiorum minus malos eos fuisse dicamus et hanc esse iustitiam, cui Deus testimonium perhibet, ut quomodo dicit Propheta Sodomam iustificatam fuisse comparatione Iudaeorum, sic sanctos virtutem aliquam comparatione sceleratorum habuisse dicamus
pass_a_gloss: That all Apostles or Prophets are defined by us as not fully holy, but that we say they were less evil in comparison with worse people, and that this is the justice to which God bears testimony: as the Prophet says Sodom was justified by comparison with the Jews, so we say the saints had some virtue by comparison with criminals.
pass_b_english: They define all the apostles and prophets as not fully holy, but say that they were less evil by comparison with worse people. They say this is the righteousness to which God bears witness: just as the prophet says that Sodom was justified by comparison with the Jews, so they say that the saints showed some virtue by comparison with criminals (Ezekiel 16:46–52).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
